To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) recommendations were frequent in the sessions studied, (b) clients who returned to treatment reported high levels of implementation, and client perception of difficulties and therapist recommendation influenced implementation.

(a) clients report a high level (87%) of implementation of recommendations and that (b) the client's perception of the difficulty of implementation and the therapist's influence are predictive of the client's implementation.

(1) clients tend to implement recommendations, (2) clients tend to perceive recommendations as fit with their goals, and (3) client perception of difficulty in implementing the recommendation is a significant predictor of implementation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the process of change in psychotherapy.
the occurrence of therapist interventions and client implementation of therapist recommendations in the context of a single psychotherapy session.
the occurrence of therapist-recommendations and client-implementation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the client's perception of the difficulty of implementation and the therapist's influence are predictive of the client's implementation of recommendations.
client perceptions of difficulties and influence are predictive of client-reported implementations of therapist recommendations.
clients who perceived a therapist's recommendations to be easy to implement and to be influenced by the therapist were more likely to report implementation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

clients are likely to accept and implement therapist recommendations, and that clients' perceptions of difficulties and the therapist's influence may be useful to therapists when considering how to make recommendations.

clients are more likely to implement therapist recommendations when they are perceived to be fit, when the client perceives few difficulties of implementation, or when the client believes the therapist is influencing the implementation.

clients who perceive a high level of difficulty in implementing the recommendation and who do not perceive that their therapist is exerting influence over them tend to report lower levels of implementation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

recommendations are common and that therapists can influence client implementation of recommendations through their recommendations, the manner in which they deliver recommendations, and through other aspects of their therapeutic style.

therapists make many recommendations, and that the client's perception of the difficulty of implementing recommendations, and the therapist's influence, are important factors in the implementation of therapist recommendations.
clients implement therapist recommendations, and that client perceptions of difficulty and therapist influence are related to client implementation.
